function: above_phy, p. 6: the learned RL policy only outputs the users' priority weights (queue-aware scheduling); beamforming and SIC come from non-learned BB or CC-TLG+SCA optimization (pp. 5, 7, 11).
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Excluded as above_phy: the only learned component is the hybrid RL long-term stage, whose action is the priority weight vector (p. 6: 'the action at the t-th time slot is at = β t , where β t is the priority weight vector'), chosen from queue and channel states to maximize the hard-latency constrained effective throughput. Beamforming and SIC are solved by non-learned optimization (BB, pp. 7-9; CC-TLG with SCA, p. 11), which the RL treats as its environment (p. 5: 'The WSR maximization algorithm in the short-term stage is viewed as part of the environment for the hybrid RL algorithm'). The paper calls this 'the resource scheduling problem' (p. 3), treats NOMA beamforming as the 'physical layer scheme' steered by the weights (pp. 6-7), and benchmarks the learned stage against Q-weighted scheduling [36] (p. 13). Since beamforming and SIC are not learned, the clause for learning a physical-layer decision jointly with one above it does not apply; no_learning was not used because the method does contain a trained DNN policy, whose role is scheduling. Borderline: if the reviewer reads the learned weights as a parametrization of the beamformer (p. 6, Sec. III-D), the work would be area 3, with provisional grades q1=0 (exponential-correlation Rayleigh, p. 12), q2=0 (policy reuse from 'other similar environments' is described on p. 10 but no test in a new condition is reported), q3=1 (Q-weighted JBSO and matching-SCA, plus a single-stage DRL baseline on HLC-ET, pp. 13-14), q4=1 (CC-TLG complexity order and Table I, p. 12), q5=0 (no code or public data).
